findings.title: Forgotten bond and adhesive hostility
findings.claim: A forgotten share of the covenant can leave enmity and hatred occupying the social interval as a binding residue, so opposition becomes one way the divided groups remain attached.
findings.mechanism: The focus verb أَغْرَيْ carries the registered adhesion and incitement branches, while the wider 5:64 and 17:53 relations supply repeated hostility between groups and hostile prompting between people; their contact changes the forgotten covenant from an isolated omission into a condition that can organize social attachment through opposition.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive how the omitted covenant share and the later enmity belong to one relational movement: a bond loses its remembered content, and hostility can occupy the place where a shared bond had held people together.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading of forgotten covenant content followed by divinely set enmity remains intact. The glue is a bounded social image, not a literal material gloss, and the packet does not establish that every hostility has this cause.

epistemic.reason: The cross-run finding and all focus branches are directly supplied, while the connection targets provide exact Arabic but no target morphology; the adhesive social relation therefore remains an explicitly bounded inference.
